To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of neighbors required to ensure a connected network grows logarithmically with the number of nodes, that this growth is very slow, and that the critical constant is close to one.
the number of neighbors needed to connect a random wireless network with n nodes is Θ(log n).
the number of neighbors needed for connectivity of wireless networks is Θ(log n).
